key_insight: Regions not observed by training views produce unreliable 3D Gaussian Splatting predictions; modeling a per-particle anisotropic visibility field with spherical harmonics yields efficient, principled uncertainty estimates that enable active mapping.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of principled visibility and uncertainty quantification in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), which leads to unreliable predictions in unobserved directions and poor view-selection for mapping.
method: Define an anisotropic visibility field per Gaussian particle relative to the training views and represent it compactly using spherical harmonics.
Derive visibility-driven uncertainty measures from the anisotropic field to identify unreliable/unseen regions in the 3DGS model.
Use these uncertainty estimates to drive active mapping / view-planning, integrating efficiently into the 3DGS pipeline for targeted data collection.
impact: Provides a practical uncertainty-aware layer for 3DGS that improves reliability of reconstructions and enables efficient, targeted data acquisition—reducing wasted views and improving downstream mapping and planning.

paper_title: Uncertainty-driven 3D Gaussian Splatting Active Mapping via Anisotropic Visibility Field
paper_authors: Shangjie Xue, Jesse Dill, Dhruv Ahuja, Frank Dellaert, Panagiotis Tsiotras
